questions.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}$ at $t=1,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3+t} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1) \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t-3 \\ {t}^{2} \\ (t+1)^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have 
 

$$
(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)+5{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(2\sqrt{3+t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1)) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+t}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1)^{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2t \\ 2(t+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Hence , we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(1)+5g(1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(1)+5{g}^{′}(1) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+1}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(1-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(1) \\ 2(1+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+4g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,{t}^{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+4g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+4g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+4⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+⟨4,\,-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+4,\,\frac{1}{t}-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,0+16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1+8\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{t-4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨8\sqrt{3-t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t)⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,\pi {t}^{2},\,1-{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)-{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\sqrt{3-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-t}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-1,\,2\pi t,\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(-1)-g(-1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =2⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-(-1)}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ),\,\frac{1}{(-1)}⟩-⟨2(-1)-1,\,2\pi (-1),\,-2(-1)⟩ \\  & =2⟨-2,-\pi ,-1⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-2\pi ,-2⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2(t-1)⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2t-2⟩+⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2t-2,\,3{t}^{2}+2t-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)+h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨-t,\,0,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨-{t}^{2},0,{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩+⟨-1,0,1⟩+⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t-1,\,0,\,2t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2t[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 8 \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ 2t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t+{t}^{2}){e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ (2t-{t}^{2}){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(2u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,({u}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u(t) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(2t+2) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot 2 \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8t+8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f\cdot g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t)
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot ({t}^{3}\,i+t\,j+({t}^{2}+t)\,k)+(20t\,i-2t\,j+(2+5t)\,k)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's find ${v}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩ \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(v(t)f(t))^{′} & =v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t) \\  & =2t⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩+2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{t}^{2},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,4{t}^{2},\,2t⟩+⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2},\,2t⟩ \\  & =2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
questions.worked_solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\times g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\times g(t)+f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,3{t}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\times g(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩, \\ f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 5 & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & {t}^{4} \\ 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}t & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}t & 5 \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\times g)^{′}(t) & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩+⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩ \\  & =⟨-7{t}^{6}+5,\,6{t}^{5}-2t,\,4{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
questions.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
({f}^{′}\cdot f)^{′}(t)={f}^{″}(t)\cdot f(t)+{f}^{′}(t)\cdot {f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j+4\cdot 2t\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j+8t\,k \\ {f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t)\,k \\  & =3\cdot 2t\,i+2j+8\,k \\  & =6t\,i+2j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{′}\cdot f)^{′}(0) & ={f}^{″}(0)\cdot f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)\cdot {f}^{′}(0) \\  & =(6(0)\,i+2\,j+8\,k)\cdot (({0}^{3}-1)\,i+({0}^{2}-2)\,j+4(0)^{2}\,k)+(3(0)^{2}\,i+2(0)\,j+8(0)\,k)\cdot (3(0)^{2}\,i+2(0)\,j+8(0)\,k) \\  & =(2\,j+8\,k)\cdot (-i-2\,j) \\  & =0(-1)+2(-2)+(0) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t)$ with respect to $t,$ where $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i-(\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k \\ g(t) & =(4t-1)\,i+{e}^{3t}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t))' = \mathbf f'(t) + 2\mathbf g'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,k \\  & =8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k, \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)k \\  & =4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+2g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+2{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k)+2(4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k) \\  & =8(t+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}+6{e}^{3t})\,j-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where $[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]$ and $u(t) = t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)g(t)+u(t){g}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+t\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem: Find $(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t),$ if $\mathbf f(u) = \ln u \, \mathbf i + (u^2+5) \, \mathbf j + 4u \, \mathbf k$ and $u(t) =2t^3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t) = \mathbf{f}'(u(t)) u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡u)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2}+5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(4u)k \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\,i+2u\,j+4\,k, \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\,i+2u(t)\,j+4\,k){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{3}}\,i+2(2{t}^{3})\,j+4\,k)\cdot 6{t}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}\,i+24{t}^{5}\,j+24{t}^{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
canonical_examples.problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{t}^{2}j \\ g(t) & =\frac{1}{t}i+{e}^{t}j\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}f(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+2t\,j, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}g(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
}
$$
